sections.title: What You'll Learn
sections.content:
Ready to learn **The String Type**?

Here's what we'll cover:

• Creating and using String objects
• Why this matters for your coding journey
• Hands-on examples you can try

sections.title: Core Concepts
sections.content:
Think of **The String Type** like building blocks. 

Every great program starts with small, simple pieces. This is one of those essential pieces!

• Start simple, then build up
• Practice makes it click
• Don't worry if it takes time - totally normal!

sections.title: Code Examples
examples:
String s1 = "Hello";
String s2 = "World";

System.out.println(s1.length());          // 5
System.out.println(s1.charAt(0));         // H
System.out.println(s1.concat(" " + s2));  // Hello World
System.out.println(s1.toUpperCase());     // HELLO
System.out.println(s1.indexOf('l'));      // 2
System.out.println(s1.substring(1, 3));   // el

sections.title: Key Points
points: Strings are objects of the String class and are immutable (cannot be changed after creation)
length() returns the number of characters; charAt(i) returns the character at index i
substring(begin, end) extracts a portion of the string from begin to end-1
equals() compares string content; == compares references (use equals for value comparison)
concat(), toUpperCase(), toLowerCase(), trim(), and replace() return new String objects

sections.title: Summary
sections.content: The String Type - Creating and using String objects. Master basics before advancing. Practice with the examples. Builds foundation for what's next.
